record.original_question: Is the following conjecture true? Conjecture A72 ([S11k]). Let b, c ∈ Z. For any n ∈ Z+ we have n−1∑ k=0 (8ck + 4c + b)Tk(b, c 2)2(b − 2c)2(n−1−k) ≡ 0 (mod n). If p is an odd prime not dividing b(b − 2c), then p−1∑ k=0 (8ck + 4c + b) Tk(b, c 2)2 (b − 2c)2k ≡ p(b + 2c) (b2 − 4c2 p ) (mod p2).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $b$ and $c$, define the generalized central trinomial coefficients $T_k(b,c)$ by
$$T_k(b,c) = [x^k]\,(x^2 + bx + c)^k = \sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor k/2 \rfloor} \binom{k}{2j}\binom{2j}{j} b^{k-2j} c^{j},$$
so that $T_k(b,c)$ is the coefficient of $x^k$ in $(x^2+bx+c)^k$.

Prove or disprove the following two assertions.

(i) For all integers $b,c$ and every positive integer $n$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} (8ck + 4c + b)\, T_k(b,c^2)^2\, (b-2c)^{2(n-1-k)} \equiv 0 \pmod{n}.$$

(ii) For every odd prime $p$ with $p \nmid b(b-2c)$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1} (8ck + 4c + b)\, T_k(b,c^2)^2\, (b-2c)^{2k} \equiv p(b+2c)\left(\frac{b^2-4c^2}{p}\right) \pmod{p^2},$$
where $\left(\frac{\cdot}{p}\right)$ denotes the Legendre symbol.
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a published proof or disproof of this specific conjecture (involving the weighted sum of squared generalized central trinomial coefficients $T_k(b,c^2)^2$ with weight $8ck+4c+b$). Many of Z.-W. Sun's conjectures on supercongruences for trinomial-type sums have been studied, but the current status of this particular pair of statements is not clearly established by the available evidence.
